newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Sellers send Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Sellers send Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: The Australian share market was sold down across the board, closing lower on Tuesday as sellers emerged to lock in profits in the absence of any countervailing overseas or local leads.
The All Ordinaries index lost 17.8 points to 2,409.1.

Over-eager early buying in the banks saw the benchmark make a brief foray into positive territory, but sellers quickly took the opportunity to douse the spark, cashing-in profits made since the mid-December rally commenced.
"There was not much of a guide or lead from overseas and the market drifted accordingly," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at Intersuisse.
He said the leaders had seen good gains recently and that the selling reflected the desire to lock in profits rather than any sea-change in sentiment.
"It's really just a case of profit-taking around the market. Most of these leading stocks are still running at a profit for people who bought at the right time."
The losses were broadly spread with both industrials and resources groupings losing about 0.75 percent.
In the miners, market bellwether BHP and WMC suffered most.
BHP scrip slid 1.8 percent to close at A$17.43 (US$13.34) but was still more than three percent up on its mid-December lows when the market started to rally to its record highs set in mid-January.
WMC shares told a similar story, closing 1.4 percent lower at A$7.95 but still more than nine percent above mid-December's lows.
In the industrials, the big banks were the feature, soaring early as eager buyers pushed the majors back into record territory but then slumping as profit takers saw opportunities.
National Australia Bank was an obvious illustration, jumping back to the A$16.00 mark initially before closing more than one percent lower at A$15.70.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
